newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Blair pledges to retain veto in EU.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Blair pledges to retain veto in EU.

text.p: Opposition Labour party leader Tony Blair said on Sunday Britain would retain the veto in key European Union policy areas if he wins the next election.
Blair was eager to counter the ruling Conservatives who say he would be a submissive "soft touch" in Europe if he wins the election that Prime Minister John Major must call by next May.

The Labour leader, overwhelming favourite in opinion polls to be the next British premier, said he would retain national control in the European Union in such areas as defence, taxation, immigration and border controls.
"That is clear and that is absolute and nobody's in any doubt about that in the rest of Europe," Blair told BBC Radio.
At this weekend's EU summit in Dublin, Major presented a list of policies that his government would not accept. That left him isolated and in opposition to most of the bloc.
Blair said: "The internal problems of the Conservative Party simply dictate Britain's position. Now that is not a healthy position for us to be in."
Citing the clash with Europe over the mad cow disease ban on British beef, he said: "There is a classic example of where Britain is marginalised, unable to proceed properly in Europe."
He said Labour would ensure that the British were "strong, leading players" in Europe, playing a constructive role.

But he stressed: "If it is in Britain's interests to be isolated through the use of the national veto, then we will be isolated. If it is in Britain's interest to be in a minority of one, we will be in a minority of one."
